text: The FDA just approved Merck's once-daily pill, the first oral version of a class defined by injectable monoclonal antibodies.
The problem those injectables never solved was adherence, needles, biweekly dosing, specialty pharmacy friction.
A daily pill routes through standard retail pharmacy.
AstraZeneca was in the same race. Now they trail.
The real signal is bigger than cholesterol.
If a monoclonal antibody mechanism can be reformulated into an FDA-approved pill, every injectable biologic in chronic care becomes an oral disruption target.
The full read on what this means for GLP-1s, IL-17, and Merck's cardio franchise is in this week's BioIntel brief.
